title: The Watch — Sc075: giant smug Richard hogs the controller while Gumball melts down

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Three-character staging on one locked living-room plate, with the acting deliberately unbalanced: Richard sits huge and motionless centre-left, smug and half-lidded, holding the game controller for the full 78 frames, while the performance is pushed onto the smallest figure — Gumball's face comps cycle worried, grimacing, screaming and finally tongue-out disgust, and Darwin holds one flat side-eye as the timing foil. Construction is one scene layer per character (DAD / GB / Darwin) over a single background, so each reaction clock can be retimed independently; the controller is a reused library prop, not a scene-specific drawing.
notes: Richard's expression never changes in 78 frames — the joke is his stillness against Gumball's escalating face-comp performance (GB headcomp 803 kf, the largest symbol in the scene).
The game controller is a shared cross-episode prop — GB118GOONS_PROPS_GAME_CONTROLLER_FINAL.fxg, from GB118 'The Goons' — placed on its own CONTROL scene layer.
Darwin is the control group: the same flat, unimpressed side-eye in every sampled frame while Gumball cycles worried, grimace, scream and tongue-out disgust.
Face comps hold 4,179 kf vs 1,119 body-puppet kf — a reaction scene carried almost entirely by the face system.
